### One-line thesis

The prior week's defensive/precious-metals impulse reversed hard: Energy and oil staged a violent snapback (XLE +7.67%, USO +7.31% 5d) while Gold and Silver's rally decelerated to near-flat (+0.76%/+1.70% 5d, down from +7.25%/+9.82%) and credit flipped back risk-on (HY beat IG by 0.53pp) — this looks like unwind of last week's flight-to-safety trade back into cyclicals, with Tech's 5d momentum fading even as its 20d trend (+8.21%) remains the strongest in the sector board.

### Cycle stance

**Yield curve data incomplete this week — 10Y is missing from the feed.** 3M sits at 3.697% (down ~1.3bp from 3.710% last week), 5Y at 4.362%, 30Y at 5.265%. Without a 10Y print, the 3m/10y spread cannot be computed this week; treat curve-shape conclusions from last week (95.0bp, bull-flattening) as stale until the 10Y series is confirmed next week. The front end's small downward drift is only a mild dovish tell on its own.

**Dollar downtrend has stalled.** DXY at 99.67, 5d return flipped to +0.07% — the first non-negative weekly print in this series — while 20d (-1.26%) still shows the broader decline intact. This is consistent with a front end that isn't backing up further; the "dovish overshoot unwind" from two weeks ago looks like it's largely run its course, and the dollar is now searching for a floor rather than extending down.

**Credit flipped back risk-on, reversing last week's defensive tilt.** HYG +0.13% vs LQD -0.40% 5d — HY outperformed IG by 0.53pp, the opposite signal from last week's 0.12pp risk-off tilt. Combined with the metals deceleration, this directly undercuts last week's "modest defensive rotation" read: whatever flight-to-safety impulse was building has reversed within a single week.

**Equity leadership rotated again — this time into Energy, away from Materials and Discretionary.** XLE swung from -3.44% 5d (deepening downtrend) to +7.67% 5d / +7.33% 20d, tracking oil's own reversal (USO +7.31% 5d after -8.66% the prior week). XLB gave back last week's +4.82% snap, printing -0.61% 5d (still +4.04% 20d) — confirming last week's flagged risk that the Materials reversal was a one-week squeeze, not new leadership. XLY turned negative for the first time in this run (-1.38% 5d), a third straight week of deceleration from +6.11% → +3.25% → -1.38%, now looking like a genuine fade rather than noise. XLK cooled sharply on the week (+1.09% 5d, down from +7.20%) but its 20d trend (+8.21%) is now the strongest in the board — last week's leadership claim gets partial confirmation on trend, but the immediate momentum has clearly faded. XLU broke its three-week losing streak (+1.61% 5d) though 20d (-1.90%) is still negative — early-stage stabilization, not yet a trend change.

**Commodities: metals stall, energy complex reverses up.** Gold +0.76% 5d / +8.98% 20d and Silver +1.70% 5d / +15.16% 20d — both decisively decelerated from last week's violent rally, essentially flat on the week even as the 20d trend stays strongly positive. This falsifies neither the "sharpest rally" framing nor confirms a reversal outright — it's a stall, and next week's print will be the tell. Oil (USO) reversed hard positive (+7.31% 5d, +2.13% 20d), confirming last week's risk #5 that the "deepening downtrend" was overstated capitulation near a bottom. Natural gas improved to +1.85% 5d (still -5.61% 20d).

**Fed posture:** With the 10Y missing this week, the cleanest read comes from the front end (3M essentially flat, -1.3bp) and the risk-asset rotation (credit risk-on, energy/cyclicals bid, metals stalling) — collectively a modestly more risk-friendly tape than last week, though the missing curve data means this call carries more uncertainty than usual.

**Curve:** Unavailable this week (10Y data missing from feed) — last confirmed read was 95.0bp (2026-08-07), bull-flattened. Needs reconfirmation next week.

### Risks / what would change my mind

1. **Energy's reversal is a one-week oil-driven snapback.** XLE (+7.67%) and USO (+7.31%) both moved sharply after multi-week declines. If either turns negative next week, this was short-covering off an oversold bottom, not new leadership.

2. **Gold/silver resume their rally rather than continuing to stall.** 5d returns collapsed from +7-10% to near-flat (+0.76%/+1.70%). If GLD/SLV 5d returns snap back above +3% next week, the "stall" read was premature and the breakout is intact; if they turn negative, last week's rally was a blow-off top.

3. **Curve data remains unavailable or shows a large gap-fill move.** The 10Y was missing this week; if it reappears sharply above or below the 4.660% level from two weeks ago, last week's bull-flattening call needs to be revisited entirely rather than assumed to have continued.

4. **Credit's risk-on re-flip doesn't persist.** HY beat IG by only 0.53pp — a modest move after an equally modest risk-off week. If IG re-outperforms HY next week, credit is chopping sideways with no directional signal, not flipping regimes weekly.

5. **XLY's deceleration reverses.** Three straight weeks of fading momentum (+6.11% → +3.25% → -1.38%) is a trend, but a single bounce back to positive would suggest this was noise around a still-intact uptrend rather than genuine rotation out of Discretionary.
